zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 8; they obstruct the view downward from Decks 8, 9, and 10, with Deck 8 cabins sitting at boat level experiencing the most obstruction.
zones.effect: You see the lifeboat roof instead of the water directly below, but the horizon and sea views remain clear; forward and aft cabins are less affected than mid-ship.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want an unobstructed view straight down to the water; irrelevant to those focused on horizon views or who accept this as normal cruise ship design.

zones.what: The main pool deck (Aqua Park) is on Deck 14 directly above Deck 13 mid and aft sections.
zones.effect: Daytime noise from pool activities, deck chairs moving, music, and foot traffic; activity continues into the evening.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for light sleepers or anyone in the cabin during the day; less important for guests who are out exploring when the pool is busy.

zones.what: The Savannah buffet (Deck 13 aft) sits directly above Deck 12 aft cabins.
zones.effect: Early morning noise starting around 6:00 AM with setup, plus foot traffic and activity throughout breakfast and lunch service.
zones.mattersTo: Critical for those wanting to sleep past 6:30 AM; not an issue for early risers or guests who breakfast elsewhere.

zones.what: The Royal Theatre spans Decks 5, 6, and 7 below the forward sections of Decks 9-12.
zones.effect: Evening show noise (music, bass) typically 8:00-11:00 PM on show nights, felt most on Deck 9, diminishing higher up.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to early-to-bed guests on show evenings; minimal impact if you're attending shows or out late anyway.

zones.what: The Safari Lounge nightclub is on Deck 7, directly below Deck 13 forward (two decks intervene: 8-12 forward are offset).
zones.effect: Late-night bass and vibration possible until 2:00-3:00 AM, though the distance and intervening structure attenuate it significantly.
zones.mattersTo: Potentially affects very sensitive sleepers; most guests report minimal disturbance given the vertical separation.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks are located mid-ship on all main cabin decks, with secondary banks forward and aft.
zones.effect: Mid-ship cabins near elevators offer excellent convenience but experience hallway traffic and bell chimes at all hours; end-of-corridor cabins are quieter but require longer walks.
zones.mattersTo: Convenience matters to those with mobility concerns or heavy port-day schedules; noise-sensitive guests should avoid cabins immediately adjacent to elevator lobbies.

zones.what: Engine room and propulsion machinery sit below and behind the aft-most cabins on Decks 8 and 9.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and hum, particularly noticeable when the ship is maneuvering or at full speed; Deck 8 aft typically feels more than Deck 9.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for vibration-sensitive sleepers; many guests don't notice or consider it the 'heartbeat' of the ship and don't mind.

zones.what: Bow thrusters are located forward at the lower decks, affecting the forward-most cabins on Decks 5 and 8 during port maneuvering.
zones.effect: Loud thruster noise during docking and departure, typically early morning and late afternoon; brief but intense.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers in port-heavy itineraries with early arrivals; thrusters only operate during maneuvering, not at sea.

zones.what: Mid-ship balcony cabins on Decks 9-12 have balconies that cantilever outward past the lifeboat line.
zones.effect: These balconies are wider than standard and offer unobstructed views past the lifeboats with no view-blocking below; they sit at the ship's center of motion for the smoothest ride.
zones.mattersTo: Excellent value for balcony seekers wanting clear views without paying for upper decks; the steadiest ride benefits those prone to seasickness.

zones.what: MSC Yacht Club area is exclusive to Decks 15 and 16 forward, with private pool, lounge, restaurant, and controlled access.
zones.effect: Complete separation from main ship traffic with dedicated elevators and facilities; quiet and private but geographically isolated from main entertainment venues.
zones.mattersTo: Perfect for guests prioritizing exclusivity and willing to pay premium; requires walks or elevator rides to main dining and shows.

Whether anchor chain noise affects specific forward cabins on Deck 5 during early port arrivals—depends on chain locker placement relative to cabin soundproofing
Degree of galley noise/odor transmission to Deck 12 cabins near the Savannah buffet pantry areas—ventilation design specifics not confirmed
